title: Piron's violin and her first sense of Jelly's playing
summary: Piron played supper club parties; she did not realize Jelly's fame until Fate Marable's boat; his light touch.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: There weren't so many piano players down here. I guess a lot of those bands didn't use piano, but... Well, no, because Piran was a violinist, you know.

He played violin. Yes. And he really played. He's old. I worked at a place after I came back from Chicago, because I was going to school in the daytime, and I'd have to work at evening because I had to support my kids, you know, my son. And I worked in a place they used to call it Bucktown. Oh, yes, out by the lake. And he played it for special parties, you know, dinner parties. It was really and truly a supper club. They didn't have any hanky-pankies going on there, like you would say, no entertainment, just the violin, that's all.
And he played beautiful music. When you first heard your brother, did he sound unusually good to you? Were you surprised that he played that well, or did it... Well, I just really intrigued him.
I didn't have any conception of music through the band.
You hadn't heard of any other pianist. You didn't know that he was much better than anything. That's right.
Not until Faden Maribor came down here with the steamer capsule, then I realized then how famous...
But your brother was so much better than anybody else that I know.
I mean, he had a different touch on him.
A little light touch and just get over the key, just to play everything, and so easy. And there was long feet, there was long legs and long arms.
